files.content: # Blueprint — Style Prompt > An engineering drawing that comes alive on one sheet of cyanotype paper: white technical line work on uneven Prussian blue, drawn in drafting order, with part balloons that ride on moving parts and notes that write themselves. The camera reads the sheet like an eye, the designed object acts through its parts, a hand shadow with a glowing pen revises the drawing, and once, only once, a drawing symbol leaves the paper and becomes real. ## 1. Essence, and what it is not - **The whole video happens on one sheet** (3200 × 2200 sheet units). The camera moves over it in continuous moves; there are no cuts inside a section. The sheet carries everything: a header with a double underline, a GENERAL NOTES column, a parts list, the figure, dimension lines, revision marks and a title-block verdict. - **A 2D line-drawing language.** Front elevation with a cabinet-oblique depth of 0.42: solids and trusses are drawn as two faces offset diagonally (back face up-right, front face down-left), which gives thickness without any 3D rendering. - **Rigorous convention carries the tone.** The drawing is dry and exact (centre lines, hidden lines, 45° hatching, numbered balloons); the notes carry wit, warmth or gravity. - **The designed thing is the character.** An object, machine, building or plan acts through its parts: an arm lifts hopefully, sags when it fails, snaps upright with joy. People appear only as a hand shadow with a pen tip, or as initials. Not a glowing hologram HUD (no wireframe glow, no 3D orbit), not a whiteboard (no marker on white), not an engraving (no tonal burin hatching as the whole look), not an infographic (one figure, one sheet, no dashboard). ## 2. Materials & rendering - **Sheet**: cyanotype painted once as a texture, in sheet coordinates, from the original shader's formula: `m = 0.10 + 0.95·(n1 − 0.25) + 0.22·(n2 − 0.5) + 0.14·(n3 − 0.5) + 0.18·x/3200`, where n1 is fbm at 760 units (slow fading), n2 is fbm stretched 1500 × 70 (horizontal coating streaks) and n3 is fbm at 190 (blotches); colour = mix(dark blue, light blue, m). Then fibres (×0.955–1.03 per pixel), a cross fold through the sheet centre (±6% bright/dark edge, a worn dashed white line on the fold), small dark specks, and a screen vignette that darkens the corners by about 24%. Paint it at a quarter resolution and only move it. - **Lines**: pale blue-white, four weights in sheet units: outline 3.2, detail 2.0, thin 1.25, hair 0.9. **Screen width = sheet width × zoom^0.65**, so close-ups do not turn into sausages and wides do not vanish (in SVG: `stroke-width: calc(w × var(--k))` with `--k = zoom^-0.35`, changed in a few steps, never every frame). - **Dash conventions** (sheet units): centre line 34 7 6 7, hidden 11 7, phantom 30 6 5 6 5 6. Hatching at 45°, spacing 8–14, hair weight. - **Occlusion by painter's order**: a solid's front face is filled with paper before its outline (the head block, balloon circles), so lines behind it disappear. - **Trusses**: two rails in outline weight, rungs and alternating diagonals in detail weight, drawn twice (back face, then front face) with the oblique offset (±8.9 units for a 60-unit-deep mast, ±6.5 for a boom). - **Balloons**: circle radius 22, thin weight, paper-filled, number in hand lettering at 1.05 × radius; a hair leader with a 3.2-unit dot on the part. Balloons fly with their parts and keep their numbers upright. - **Hand shadow**: blurred strokes, not a silhouette: the pen (radius 7) from the nib up-right to (200, −330), four fingers (radius 14–16), a palm (62) and a forearm (58) further up-right; each part's shadow is offset by (34, 46) × its height above the paper, so the higher parts fall further down-right. Blur 8 for the pen, 16 for the hand; it darkens the paper and the lines under it by about 30%. - **The one real thing** (once, at the peak): a drawing symbol gets soft volume (one gradient across the whole shape, light from the top-left), a soft white glow, and light or shadow falling across the lines; its drawn outline stays on the paper as a pale imprint. In the example the light rays of a lamp become real light: a blurred cone, a glowing bulb, a pool on the desk line. - **Rubber stamp**: double border (outer 9, inner 3, 14 inset), heavy technical capitals, rotated −8°, ink with speckled gaps, landing with a 0.35 s camera bump. ## 3. Colour logic - **Blue and white only**, plus one stamp colour used exactly once. - `--latar` is the paper. The two blues of the coating are mixed from it: dark = `--latar` 88% toward black (≈ #18336b), light = `--latar` lifted in OKLCH lightness by 0.09 with 1.2× chroma (≈ #2a58a6). A pale brand therefore gets a whiteprint (white sheet, grey mottling), a dark brand a night-blue sheet. - `--teks` is the line work and the hand lettering (lines are `--teks` 94% over the paper, hair lines and hatching 80%). `--teks-redup` carries secondary lettering: the subtitle line under the header, the parenthesised remark, part-list headings. - `--latar-2` is the NOTE box fill (navy, at 64% over the sheet); its lettering is `--teks`. - `--utama` is the brand's signal and plays the stamp ink; as lettering on the sheet it is always drawn with `--utama-di-latar` (a lighter red in the example, the text colour on a pale brand). Nothing else on the sheet is coloured. - `--aksen` only tints the halo of the glowing pen nib. - Fixed: the hand shadow is the paper mixed toward black; the real light is white with 8% of `--utama`, so on a white sheet it nearly disappears while the drawn lamp still reads. Reference colours from the film: paper #1e3b78 (64% of the frame), shadowed paper #193468, lines #e7f0f9, note box rgba(12, 28, 62, 0.58), stamp red #c23b2e. ## 4. Type - `--font-judul` sets the sheet header: hand lettering (Patrick Hand), 132 sheet units with 14 units of letter spacing, upper case, an outline-weight underline 32 units below the baseline and a hair underline 10 units under that. At the working zoom (about 0.8) that is about 105 px on screen, cropped by the frame edge like a real sheet. - `--font-isi` sets the NOTE subtitles: Patrick Hand 38 px on screen, line height 46, wrapped by hand at about 30 characters (the box never grows past ~700 px). - Look tokens the brand does not replace: `--font-tangan` (Patrick Hand) for everything lettered on the drawing — GENERAL NOTES items 25, the parenthesised remark and REV note 30, balloons 23, live annotations 28 — always upper case; `--font-teknik` (Inter) for the technical sans: the status line 600 at 40 with 8 letter spacing, the subtitle line 400 at 25 with 2, column headings 600 at 22–26 with 3, the NOTE cell 600 at 15 and its number 800 at 30, the stamp 800 at 56 with 8; `--font-paraf` (Caveat 700, 34) for initials only. - Hand lettering for notes, technical sans for fields: never the other way round. A wider brand font for `--font-isi` wraps the NOTE sooner: shorten the line rather than shrinking it. ## 5. Motion quality The original runs on a 108 BPM grid (beat 0.556 s); the example stretches it by 1.25 (beat 0.694 s) and keeps its proportions. - **Draw-on**: lines are revealed by arc length (`stroke-dashoffset`, ease power1.inOut) with a glowing nib at the head. **Drafting order**: centre lines → outlines → detail → hatching → dimensions → balloons → labels, items staggered 0.1–0.15 s inside a layer, each layer starting on a beat. In the example the arm draws in 0.3–1.5 s: centre line 0.4 s, rails 0.6 s, diagonals 0.55 s, shade 0.5 s, mesh 0.45 s, hatching 0.4 s, balloons 0.25 s each 0.15 s apart. - **Lettering**: every text is written left to right behind a clip with a nib: a NOTE line in 0.35 s, a GENERAL NOTES item in 1.5 s (with its subtitle, 0.2 s after it), a REV note in 0.63 s, initials in 0.25 s. A NOTE box fades in 0.2 s, holds at least max(1.8 s, the line plus 0.6 s), fades in 0.2 s. - **Machine acting** (monotone cubic keys, from the original's boom track): hopeful lift +16° over 1.5 s, two small bobs (−3.4°, +2.3°, −1.7° every 0.6–0.75 s), then **failure**: the part sags 46° over 1.75 s, fastest at the end, rebounds 2.3° in 0.6 s and settles 0.75 s later. **Joy**: snaps back 32° in 0.25 s, overshoots by 3° and settles in another 0.25 s. - **Mechanisms step on the grid** like an escapement: one tooth per eighth note, landing with an ease-out over the first 35% of the step; when the machine fails they slow over ~1.5–2 s and stop, and live readouts count down with them. - **Hand**: enters from bottom-right in 0.6 s (ease-out cubic) while fading in 0.4 s; follows the pen exactly (a revision cloud is drawn scallop by scallop, 15 scallops in 1.25 s, the hand riding 20 units outside each scallop with an 18-unit bounce per scallop); exits bottom-right in 0.9 s (ease-in cubic) while fading out. - **The real thing**: two breaths first (opacity 0.22 then 0.32, about 0.25 s each, on consecutive beats), then it becomes real over 0.5 s (power3.inOut). Nothing else happens on the sheet during the breaths. - **Stamp**: lands in 0.12 s at 94% → 90% scale, the camera bumps 5 px for 0.35 s (a damped 90 rad/s sine). - Endings hold still at least 2 s, then fade 0.5 s. ## 6. Camera grammar Camera = a centre point in sheet units plus a zoom; screen = (point − centre) × zoom + screen centre. Keys are interpolated with monotone cubic curves, so moves start and stop without overshoot. | Move | What it expresses | Can serve | |---|---|---| | Close-up (zoom 1.85) climbing the figure while pulling back to 0.78 over ~3.7 s | the design being discovered, part by part | the opening; naming the object | | Medium-wide, figure ~2/3 of the height at left, empty sky right, header cropped at the top-left | the drawing as a whole; room for notes | stating facts; the flaw (the emptiness is the joke) | | Slow drift (≈ 3% of the frame per second, zoom 0.77–0.82) | the eye keeps reading | any hold while things are lettered | | Locked-off while the hand draws | deliberation | a revision; a decision | | Slow push-in, ×1.3 over ~1.8 s, onto the real thing | wonder | the one real thing; the verdict | | 2× close-up cut on a downbeat | the mechanism's heart | gears meshing; a joint; a valve | | Track along a path of force (chain, pipe, wire) | cause and effect | how it works; a sequence of operations | | Whole sheet on the dark table | scale, the document as an object | an opening or a final verdict | | Lateral pan Fig. 1 → Fig. 2 → Fig. 3 | versions, steps, time | revisions; stages of construction | Keep storytelling shots close; whole-sheet wides are rare. Keep the main figure at least 960/zoom from any sheet edge you will frame. Transitions are cuts on downbeats or figure-number rewrites, never dissolves. The stamp is the only camera bump. ## 7. Native moves - **Drafting order.** The object draws itself the way an engineer would, a layer per beat, a glowing nib at each head while the camera pulls back. *Fits content like:* a desk lamp built from bicycle parts; a violin in a luthier's class; a creator's camera rig; the house in the first scene of a story. - **Machine acting.** A part is the face: it lifts hopefully, sags over 1.5–2 s with a small rebound when it fails, snaps upright with an overshoot when it works; readouts follow it. *Fits content like:* a sagging shelf a furniture maker fixes; a drooping plant in a gardening class; a creator's tripod that will not stay up; a tired robot in a children's story. - **Notes that write themselves.** A NOTE box in the empty sky letters the line; the same sentence is lettered into the GENERAL NOTES column, so the final wide carries the whole script as drawing notes. *Fits content like:* the steps of a recipe class; the specs of a new product; a teacher's three rules; the narrator's lines of a fable. - **The hand revises.** A blurred hand shadow enters, draws the change, rings it with a 15-scallop revision cloud, adds a numbered delta triangle, a REV line and initials, then leaves. *Fits content like:* a bakery's second oven; a course module rewritten after feedback; a creator's redesigned thumbnail; a character's plan that changes halfway. - **Live annotations.** Dimensions measure moving parts and their numbers change; balloons fly with their parts; a section line sweeps across to reveal the inside. *Fits content like:* the reach of an adjustable arm; the angle of a solar panel; a creator's subscriber gauge; the depth of a well in a village tale. - **A symbol made real** (once, at the peak). A convention leaves the drawing language: light rays become light, a hatch becomes rain, a centre line becomes a road. It gets soft volume, glow and a shadow or light across the lines, and leaves a pale imprint. *Fits content like:* a lamp finally lit; a café's steam rising from a drawn cup; a student's first working circuit; a dream turning into a plan. - **The title block as story.** The status field is the verdict; revision rows are the history; a red stamp lands once with a camera bump. *Fits content like:* LOLOS UJI on a product; an approved permit; a graduated class; the end of a long journey. - **Fig. numbers as transitions.** "FIG. 1" struck through and rewritten "FIG. 2 · TAMPAK URAI". *Fits content like:* versions of a product; phases of a renovation; before and after a tutorial; chapters of a story. ## 8. Pitfalls - **Performance (live preview).** Never animate SVG `transform` attributes, stroke widths or many paths inside the big sheet layer: every change repaints the whole sheet. Put each moving part (arm faces, hanging parts) in its own small layer placed every frame with a CSS transform computed from the camera; keep the sheet one composited layer and re-raster it only on the frames where the camera lands (toggle `will-change` for one frame). Paint the paper once at quarter resolution into an ``. Blur only static layers (the hand shadow, the real light) that then only move or fade. - **Line weights not scaled with zoom** make sausages in close-ups and vanishing wides; but changing a width variable every frame repaints everything: use two or three steps. - **Main figure near the sheet edge** shows the desk in wides; leave 960/zoom of paper around anything you frame. - **Subtitles on the sheet** scroll away and get lost in the lines: NOTE boxes live in screen space, in the shot's empty sky (bottom-right in the example at x 1180, y 860), never over the figure; the bottom of the drawing is ground line and base. - **The real thing darkened by its own shadow**, or per-lobe shading that reads as grapes: one gradient across the whole union, one glow behind it. - **A small payoff undersells it**: the real thing at about a third of the frame height, centred, pushed in on. - **Clutter**: hand lettering at 25 sheet units is small on screen (~20 px); it is texture, not message. The message is the NOTE box (38 px) and the header. Keep 120 px left and right and 80 px top and bottom clear for the NOTE and the stamp; the header and the notes column may run off the frame like a real sheet. - **Light brands**: the sheet turns into a whiteprint; check that the hand shadow, hatching and hair lines still separate from the white, and accept that real light is nearly invisible on white (the drawn lamp and the stamp still carry the moment). - **Scripted geometry**: measure path lengths and pen paths once while building (`getTotalLength`, `getPointAtLength`), never inside the timeline callback; seeking must give the same frame in any order. ## Measured from the references - The reference shows 12 s of the original film (its 19.9–31.9 s): one continuous shot, no cuts, motion low (2.05), the palette above. Times here are ×1.25 as in the example. - Camera keys (time s: centre x, y, zoom): −0.75: 1080, 1530, 1.85 · 0.75: 1110, 980, 1.6 · 1.9: 1420, 720, 1.1 · 3.0: 1570, 790, 0.78 · 4.6: 1610, 840, 0.77 · 5.7: 1640, 860, 0.78 · 10.6: 1700, 800, 0.82 · 11.5: 1760, 740, 0.95 · 12.3: 1790, 720, 1.05. - Arm keys (time s: degrees above horizontal): 0.1: 29.8 · 1.6: 45.8 · 2.4: 42.4 · 3.0: 44.7 · 3.9: 43 · 5.6: −2.9 · 6.3: −5.2 · 7.0: −3.4 · then joy: −3.4 → 28.6 in 0.25 s → 25.8 in 0.25 s. - Sheet layout (sheet units): header baseline (170, 250); status line 340; subtitle line 382; GENERAL NOTES at (2280, 150), items from y 208, 34 per line, 14 between items; parts list ruled from (2280, 1447) in 27-unit rows; mast axis x 1100, ground line y 1860, pivot (1175, 933); boom 600 long with a 130 tail; revision cloud rx 250 × ry 120–135; delta triangle 60 wide with the REV line 60 left of it and 70 below. - Story beats of the reference window: the note states the success at 2.5 s, the remark in parentheses at 3.3–4.3 s, the part sags 3.9–5.6 s, the hand enters at 5.75 s and draws the revision 6.4–8.9 s, the REV note 8.9–10.1 s, the hand leaves by 11 s, two breaths, then the symbol becomes real and the machine snaps up.

# Blueprint: beat plan

Default length 15 s. Tempo per beat (seconds): short 1.6, medium 2.8, long 4.0.

## hook

- en: camera pulls back from 1.85× up the figure while it draws itself in drafting order: centre lines, outlines, mesh, balloons
- id: kamera mundur dari 1,85× menyusuri gambar yang menggambar dirinya urut drafter: sumbu, garis luar, jaring, balon

## problem

- en: the part acts the failure: it sags 46° over 1.75 s with a small rebound; a remark in parentheses is lettered in the empty sky
- id: bagian mesin berakting gagal: melorot 46° dalam 1,75 dtk lalu terpantul; catatan dalam kurung ditulis di langit kosong

## fact

- en: a NOTE box writes the line in the empty sky, and the same line is lettered into the GENERAL NOTES column
- id: kotak CATATAN menulis kalimatnya di langit kosong, dan kalimat yang sama ditulis di kolom CATATAN UMUM

## step

- en: a blurred hand shadow with a glowing pen draws the change, rings it with a 15-scallop revision cloud, adds REV 1 and initials
- id: bayangan tangan berpena menggambar perubahan, melingkarinya dengan awan revisi, lalu menulis REV. 1 dan paraf

## compare

- en: FIG. 1 struck through and rewritten FIG. 2 as the camera pans to the new version; a live dimension shows the new value
- id: FIG. 1 dicoret jadi FIG. 2 saat kamera bergeser ke versi baru; garis ukur menunjukkan angka barunya

## number

- en: a dimension line measures the moving part and its hand-lettered figure changes with it
- id: garis ukur mengukur bagian yang bergerak, angkanya yang ditulis tangan ikut berubah

## proof

- en: a section line sweeps across the part; the cut walls fill with 45° hatching and show what is inside
- id: garis potong menyapu bagian itu; dinding potongannya diarsir 45° dan isinya terlihat

## offer

- en: the title block is lettered in field by field: name, price, contact, the status rewritten
- id: kotak judul diisi tulisan tangan per kolom: nama, harga, kontak, status ditulis ulang

## cta

- en: the symbol turns real and glows, the part snaps up with an overshoot, a red stamp lands; contact in a NOTE, held 2 s
- id: simbol jadi nyata dan bercahaya, bagian mesin tegak lewat sasaran, cap merah jatuh; kontak di CATATAN, diam 2 dtk

## payoff

- en: once, a drawn symbol becomes real: soft volume, glow, light across the lines, a pale imprint left behind; held 2 s
- id: sekali saja, simbol gambar jadi nyata: bervolume, berpendar, cahaya jatuh di garis, jejaknya tertinggal; diam 2 dtk

<!doctype html>
<html lang="id">
  <head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=1920, height=1080" />
    <title>Cetak biru</title>
    <script src="/_lib/gsap@3.15.1/gsap.min.js"></script>
    <style>
      @font-face { font-family: "Patrick Hand"; src: url("data:font/woff2;base64,"); font-weight: 400; }
      @font-face { font-family: "Inter"; src: url("data:font/woff2;base64,"); font-weight: 400; }
      @font-face { font-family: "Inter"; src: url("data:font/woff2;base64,"); font-weight: 600; }
      @font-face { font-family: "Inter"; src: url("data:font/woff2;base64,"); font-weight: 800; }
      @font-face { font-family: "Caveat"; src: url("data:font/woff2;base64,"); font-weight: 700; }
      /* Token brand (recipes/README.md): brand mengganti dua belas nilai pertama. */
      :root {
        --latar: #1e3b78; --latar-2: #0c1c3e; --utama: #c23b2e; --aksen: #9fd3ff;
        --teks: #e7f0f9; --teks-redup: #b6c4de; --teks-di-utama: #fdf1ef; --teks-di-aksen: #0c1c3e;
        --utama-di-latar: #ff7a6b; --aksen-di-latar: #9fd3ff;
        --font-judul: "Patrick Hand", "Noto Sans", sans-serif; --font-isi: "Patrick Hand", "Noto Sans", sans-serif;
        /* Huruf gambar (tangan drafter, teknik, paraf) milik gaya, tidak diganti brand. */
        --font-tangan: "Patrick Hand", sans-serif; --font-teknik: "Inter", sans-serif; --font-paraf: "Caveat", cursive;
        /* Kertas sianotip (dua biru), tinta, bayangan, cahaya: dari token, jadi lembar ikut brand. */
        --kertas-gelap: color-mix(in oklab, var(--latar) 88%, black);
        --kertas-terang: oklch(from var(--latar) calc(l + 0.09) calc(c * 1.2) h);
        --tinta: color-mix(in oklab, var(--teks) 94%, var(--latar));
        --tinta-tipis: color-mix(in oklab, var(--teks) 80%, var(--latar));
        --bayang: color-mix(in oklab, var(--latar) 15%, black);
        --cahaya: color-mix(in oklab, var(--utama) 8%, white);
      }
      * { margin: 0; padding: 0; box-sizing: border-box; }
      html, body { width: 1920px; height: 1080px; overflow: hidden; background: var(--latar); }
      #root { position: relative; width: 100%; height: 100%; overflow: hidden; background: var(--latar); color: var(--teks); font-family: var(--font-isi); }
      /* Lapisan kamera dalam satuan lembar 3200 × 2200: layar = (titik − kamera) × zoom + tengah. */
      .cam, #vig { position: absolute; left: 0; top: 0; width: 1920px; height: 1080px; transform-origin: 0 0; }
      #paper, #lys, #light, #tangan, #pena, .part { will-change: transform; }
      .part { position: absolute; left: 0; top: 0; width: 1px; height: 1px; transform-origin: 0 0; } /* bagian bergerak: lapisan sendiri */
      #paper img { position: absolute; left: 300px; top: 60px; width: 2600px; height: 1840px; }
      #vig { background: radial-gradient(ellipse 71% 71% at 50% 50%, transparent 30%, color-mix(in oklab, black 25%, transparent)); } /* tepi 24% lebih gelap */
      svg { position: absolute; left: 0; top: 0; overflow: visible; }
      /* Empat tebal garis; --k = zoom^-0,35, jadi lebar di layar = lebar × zoom^0,65. */
      .ink * { fill: none; stroke: var(--tinta); stroke-linecap: round; stroke-linejoin: round; stroke-width: calc(2.3px * var(--k, 1)); }
      .ink .o { stroke-width: calc(3.6px * var(--k, 1)); }
      .ink .t { stroke-width: calc(1.45px * var(--k, 1)); }
      .ink .h { stroke-width: calc(1.05px * var(--k, 1)); stroke: var(--tinta-tipis); }
      .ink .c { stroke-dasharray: 34 7 6 7; } .ink .s { stroke-dasharray: 11 7; } /* sumbu, tersembunyi */
      .ink .lipat { stroke: color-mix(in oklab, var(--teks) 34%, var(--latar)); stroke-width: 2.6px; stroke-dasharray: 16 10 4 12; }
      .ink .isi { fill: var(--latar); } .ink .dot { fill: var(--tinta); stroke: none; }
      .ink text { fill: var(--teks); stroke: none; font: 23px var(--font-tangan); text-anchor: middle; dominant-baseline: central; }
      /* Huruf ditulis kiri ke kanan; ujung pena bercahaya berjalan selebar tulisan. */
      .w { position: relative; width: fit-content; white-space: nowrap; } .tx { display: block; } .abs { position: absolute; }
      .nib { position: absolute; left: 0; top: 55%; width: 100%; height: 0; visibility: hidden; }
      .nib::before, #pena { content: ""; position: absolute; width: 34px; height: 34px; border-radius: 50%; background: radial-gradient(circle, white 0 12%, color-mix(in oklab, var(--aksen) 45%, transparent) 25%, transparent 70%); }
      .nib::before { left: -17px; top: -17px; }
      #pena, #tangan { left: 0; top: 0; visibility: hidden; }
      .tangan { font-family: var(--font-tangan); text-transform: uppercase; }
      .teknik { font-family: var(--font-teknik); font-weight: 600; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 3px; }
      #kop h1 { font: 400 132px/1 var(--font-judul); letter-spacing: 14px; text-transform: uppercase; border-bottom: 3.2px solid var(--tinta); padding-bottom: 6px; }
      #kop h1::after { content: ""; position: absolute; left: 0; right: 0; bottom: -11px; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--tinta); }
      #kop .st { margin-top: 26px; font: 600 40px/1 var(--font-teknik); letter-spacing: 8px; }
      #kop .sb { margin-top: 16px; font: 400 25px/1 var(--font-teknik); letter-spacing: 2px; color: var(--teks-redup); }
      #umum { width: 740px; font-size: 25px; line-height: 34px; } #umum p { margin-bottom: 14px; }
      #umum h2 { width: 300px; padding-bottom: 6px; border-bottom: 1.25px solid var(--tinta); font-size: 26px; line-height: 26px; margin-bottom: 32px; }
      .pl { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 62px 528px 180px 70px; grid-auto-rows: 27px; font-size: 19px; line-height: 27px; }
      .pl b { font: 600 15px/27px var(--font-teknik); color: var(--teks-redup); } .pl span { padding-left: 10px; }
      #turun, #rev { font-size: 30px; } #turun { color: var(--teks-redup); transform: translateX(-50%); }
      .paraf { margin-top: 4px; font: 700 34px/1 var(--font-paraf); text-transform: none; }
      /* Cap karet: satu-satunya warna di luar biru-putih, sekali, membawa putusan. */
      #cap { left: 2010px; top: 637px; height: 106px; padding: 0 34px 0 40px; border: 7px solid var(--utama-di-latar); color: var(--utama-di-latar); visibility: hidden; white-space: nowrap;
        box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 7px var(--latar), inset 0 0 0 10px var(--utama-di-latar); font: 800 56px/92px var(--font-teknik); letter-spacing: 8px; }
      #lys { visibility: hidden; clip-path: polygon(-3000px -3000px, 9000px -3000px, 9000px 1860px, -3000px 1860px); }
